ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure is triangle ABC, point J is inside the triangle. Point D is on BC, point E is on AB, point F is on AC, and the right-angle markings in the figure show that JD is perpendicular to BC, JE is perpendicular to AB, and JF is perpendicular to AC. The figure also marks AJ = 15 and AE = 12. Reasoning: Because the problem gives that J is the incenter, the perpendicular distances from J to the three sides are equal, that is, JD = JE = JF. Using right triangle AJE, in which AJ is the hypotenuse, AE = 12, and AJ = 15, so JE = sqrt(15^2 - 12^2) = sqrt(225 - 144) = sqrt(81) = 9. Therefore JF = JE = 9.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as triangle ABC with interior point J. The right-angle markers show JD ⟂ BC, JE ⟂ AB, and JF ⟂ AC; the side labels show AJ = 15 and AE = 12 in right triangle AJE. From the text, use that J is the incenter, so its perpendicular distances to the sides of the triangle are equal: JD = JE = JF. Compute JE using the Pythagorean theorem in right triangle AJE: JE = sqrt(AJ^2 - AE^2) = sqrt(15^2 - 12^2) = 9. Therefore JF = 9.
